Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY DILG OPINION NO. 33 S. 2010 18 March 2010 MR. PERCIVAL QUINAN Punong Barangay Barangay Boboy, Agno, Pangasinan Dear PB Quinan. This pertains to your letter requesting opmion from this Department on issues involving a resolution passed by the Sangguniang Bayan of Agno, Pangasinan imposing upon you the penalty of removal as Punong Barangay of Barangay Boboy of the said municipality. Based on the information and documents you furnished us, it appears that on June 17, 2009, an administrative case was filed against you before the Sanggumang Bayan for acts unbecoming a public officer, dishonesty and abuse of authority. On September 28, 2009, the Sangguniang Bayan placed you under preventive suspension for 90 days. On December 16, 2009, the Sanggumang Bayan issued a resolution finding you administratively liable and imposmg upon you the penalty of removal from office, inter alia. On December 17, 2009, you recerved a copy of the resolution. On December 27, 2009, after having been advised by your counsel that the SB accordingly has no power to impose the penalty of removal from offce, you informed the barangay officials that you would be re-assummg your post effective December 28, 2009. On January 3, '2010, you presided over the first session of the Sangguniang Barangay. On January 4, 2010€you filed a motion for reconsideration on the resolution of the SB arguing that it has no authority to remove you from office. On January 5, 2010, Mr. Roger B. Amian, the MLGOO assigned in Agno, Pangasinan, Issued a certification stating that you have been reinstated as Punong Barangay since December 29, 2010. However, on January 6, 2010, Mr. Amian verbally recalled his certification in a conference called by him and stated that the first ranking barangay member would act as the p B. Given the foregoing, you now seek our opinion on the followmg issues: (I) Enforceability of the Resolution/Judgment issued by the Sangguniang Bayan of Agno, Pangasinan considermg that it does not have authority to impose the penalty of removal from office; (2) The authority of a Municipal Local Government Officer to issue a Certification and to verbally recall/revoke the said Certification; (3) Other pertment matters relative to the aforementioned scenano/events. Anent your first query. please be informed that the issue on whether or not a Sanggunian has the authority to remove from office an erring elective official from (fice has already been categorically and unequivocally laid to rest.

According to the Supreme Court in Ramir Pablico vs. Alejandro Villapando [385 SCRA 601; July 31, 2002], it is only by order of the proper court that an elective offcial can be removed from offce. That is the clear import of the last sentence of Section 60 of the Local Government Code, which provides that: "An elective offcial may be removed from offce on the grounds enumerated above by order of the proper court". While Section 61 of the same law enumerates the disciplining authorities where a complaint against an elective offcial may be filed, which includes the Sangguniang Bayan in cases involving barangay omcials, the Supreme Court made it clear that these disciplining authorities are devoid of any power of removal because said power, according to Section 60 as aforesaid, is lodged with the courts of law. The foregoing decision was further clarified in a more recent decision of the Supreme Court in the case of The Sanggumang Barangay of Barangay Don Marjano Marcos, Mumcupalit.r of Bayombong Provmee of Nueva Vizcaya vs. Punong Barangay Severmo Martinez [G.R. No. 170626 March 03, the pertinent portk)n of which reads: "However, the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang Bayan cannot order the removal of an erring elective barangay official from (fice, as the courts are exclusively vested with this power under Section 60 of the I-Æcal Government Code. Thus, if the acts allegedly committed by the barangay official are of a grave nature and, if found guilty, would merit the penalty of removal from office, the case should be filed with the regional trial court. Once the court assumes jurisdiction, it retains jurisdiction over the case even if it would be subsequently apparent during the trial that a penalty less than removal from omce is appropriate. On the other hand, the most extreme penalty that the Sanggumang Panlungsod or Sangguniang Bayan may impose on the erring elective barangay official is suspension; if it deems that the removal of the official from service IS warranted, then it can resolve that the proper charges be filed in court. Considering the above premises, the Sanggumang Bayan cannot therefore Impose upon an elective barangay official the penalty of removal from office. Should the Sangguniang Bayan render a decision imposing upon a certain elective barangay omcial the penalty of removal, such a decision is null and void for having been rendered without authority in law. Hence, In response to your first query, we opme that the ResolutionJJudgment of the Sangguniang Bayan of Agno. Pangasinan imposing upon you the penalty of removal from office was issued in excess of its authority. As a necessary consequence, said Resolution/Judgment is null and void so that it cannot be enforced it being legally non-existent. This finds basis in the following pronouncement of the Supreme Court in Nazarmo vs. Almario, et.al. [G.R. No. 111610. February 27, 20021, to wit: "A void judgment never acquires finality. Hence, while admittedly, the petitioner in the case at bar failed to appeal timely the aforementioned decision of the Municipal Trial Court of Naic, Cavite, it cannot be deemed to have become final and executory. In contemplation of law, that void decision is deemed nonexistent. Thus, there was no effective or operative judgment to appeal from. In

Metmpolitan Waterworks & Sewerage System vs. Sison, this Court held that: 'xxx [A] void judgment is not entitled to the respect accorded to a valid Judgment, but may be entirely disregarded or declared inoperative by any tribunal in which effect is sought to be given to it, It is attended by none of the consequences of a valid adjudication. It has no legal or binding effect or efficacy for any purpose or at any place. It cannot affect, impair or create rights. It is not entitled to enforcement and is, ordinarily, no protection to those who seek to enforce. All proceedings founded on the void judgment are themselves regarded as invalid. In other words, a void judgment is regarded as a nullity, and the situation is the same as it would be if there were no judgment. It, accordingly, leaves the parties litigants in the same position they were in before the trial.' Thus, a void judgment IS no judgment at all. It cannot be the source Of any right nor of any obligation. All acts performed pursuant to it and all claims emanating from it have no legal effect. Hence, it can never become final and any writ of execution based on it IS void: "xxx it may be said to be a lawless thing which can be treated as an outlaw and slain at sight, or ignored wherever and whenever it exhibits its head." Anent your second query, we opine that the certification Issued by the MLGOO reinstating you as the Punong Barangay after the expiration of the period of preventive suspension is actually of no legal significance. This is because, with or without said certification, your reinstatement as the Punong Barangay took effect by operation of law. Finally, as to the verbal recall of the MLGOO's certification, we are of the view that the same does not affect the fact that you have been reinstated as the Punong Barangay by operation of law. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: ATTY. JESU . DO Director III EIV DIR MANUEL V.
